claim: Mutations in connexin26 (Cx26) underlie a range of serious human pathologies.
source: Mutations in connexin26 (Cx26) underlie a range of serious human pathologies.
evidence: This is a general statement about established medical knowledge regarding Cx26 mutations and human disease.

claim: Cx26 hemichannels are directly opened by CO2.
source: Previously we have shown that Cx26 hemichannels are directly opened by CO2 (Meigh et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work by Meigh et al., 2013.

claim: The effects of human disease-causing mutations on the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26 are entirely unknown.
source: However the effects of human disease-causing mutations on the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26 are entirely unknown.
evidence: This statement reflects the knowledge gap that existed prior to this study.

claim: Cx26 hemichannels with the mutation A88V are CO2 insensitive.
source: Here, we report the first connection between the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26 and human pathology, by demonstrating that Cx26 hemichannels with the mutation A88V, linked to Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness syndrome, are both CO2 insensitive and associated with disordered breathing in humans.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including dye loading experiments.

claim: The A88V mutation in Cx26 is linked to Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness syndrome.
source: Here, we report the first connection between the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26 and human pathology, by demonstrating that Cx26 hemichannels with the mutation A88V, linked to Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness syndrome, are both CO2 insensitive and associated with disordered breathing in humans.
evidence: This is established medical knowledge about the association between A88V mutation and KID syndrome.

claim: Cx26 hemichannels with the A88V mutation are associated with disordered breathing in humans.
source: Here, we report the first connection between the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26 and human pathology, by demonstrating that Cx26 hemichannels with the mutation A88V, linked to Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness syndrome, are both CO2 insensitive and associated with disordered breathing in humans.
evidence: This claim is supported by the case study data presented in the manuscript.

claim: This is the first connection between the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26 and human pathology.
source: Here, we report the first connection between the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26 and human pathology, by demonstrating that Cx26 hemichannels with the mutation A88V, linked to Keratitis-Ichthyosis-Deafness syndrome, are both CO2 insensitive and associated with disordered breathing in humans.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: Puc19 Cx26A88V was produced from wild type Cx26 via the Quikchange protocol.
source: Puc19 Cx26A88V was produced from wild type Cx26 via the Quikchange protocol using the following primers: forward 5′ TGT CCA CGC CGG TCC TCC TGG TAG C 3′ reverse 5′ GCT ACC AGG AGG ACC GGC GTG GAC A 3′.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to create the mutant construct.

claim: Cx26A88V was subcloned into a pCAG-GS mCherry vector for mammalian cell transfection.
source: Cx26A88V was subcloned into a pCAG-GS mCherry vector for mammalian cell transfection.
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure performed.

claim: Sequencing confirmed successful mutation of Cx26 and verified that apart from the desired mutation the sequence was identical to the wild type.
source: Successful mutation of Cx26 was confirmed by sequencing which also verified that apart from the desired mutation the sequence was identical to the wild type.
evidence: This describes the verification of the mutant construct through sequencing data.

claim: HeLa cells were cultured in DMEM with 10% FCS and addition of 3 mM CaCl2.
source: HeLa cells were cultured by standard methods in DMEM, 10% FCS with addition of 3 mM CaCl2.
evidence: This describes the experimental cell culture conditions used.

claim: Cells were plated onto coverslips at a density of 5 × 10^4 cells per well for experimentation.
source: For experimentation, cells were plated onto coverslips at a density of 5 × 104 cells per well.
evidence: This describes the experimental plating conditions used.

claim: Transient transfections were performed using the genejuice protocol.
source: Transient transfections were performed using the genejuice protocol.
evidence: This describes the transfection method used in the experiments.

claim: Hypercapnic aCSF was saturated with sufficient CO2 to adjust the final pH to pH 7.5, matching that of the control aCSF.
source: Hypercapnic aCSF was saturated with sufficient CO2 (the remaining balance being O2) to adjust the final pH (pH 7.5) to that of the control aCSF removing any potential effects of changes in extracellular pH.
evidence: This describes the experimental design to control for pH effects.

claim: pH matching between hypercapnic and control aCSF removes any potential effects of changes in extracellular pH.
source: Hypercapnic aCSF was saturated with sufficient CO2 (the remaining balance being O2) to adjust the final pH (pH 7.5) to that of the control aCSF removing any potential effects of changes in extracellular pH.
evidence: This is an inference about the experimental design controlling for pH as a confounding variable.

claim: All non-hypercapnic solutions were saturated with 95% O2/5% CO2.
source: All other solutions were saturated with 95% O2/5% CO2.
evidence: This describes the gas composition used for control solutions.

claim: HeLa cells transiently transfected with Cx26A88V were exposed to Hypercapnic aCSF (55 mmHg or 70 mmHg) containing 200 µM CBF for 10 min.
source: Coverslips plated with HeLa cells transiently transfected with Cx26A88V were exposed to Hypercapnic aCSF (55 mmHg or 70 mmHg) containing 200 µM CBF for 10 min.
evidence: This describes the experimental dye loading protocol used.

claim: After hypercapnic exposure, cells were exposed to control aCSF with 200 µM CBF for 5 min followed by a 30 min wash with control aCSF.
source: This was followed by control aCSF with 200 µM CBF for 5 min and a 30 min wash with control aCSF to ensure that all dye is removed from the outside of the cells.
evidence: This describes the washing protocol used in the experiments.

claim: The 30 min wash with control aCSF ensures that all dye is removed from the outside of the cells.
source: This was followed by control aCSF with 200 µM CBF for 5 min and a 30 min wash with control aCSF to ensure that all dye is removed from the outside of the cells.
evidence: This is an inference about the purpose of the washing step in removing extracellular dye.

claim: A control comparison was used to establish baseline loading occurring in the absence of a stimulus.
source: A control comparison was used to establish any baseline loading occurring in the absence of a stimulus.
evidence: This describes the experimental design rationale for the control condition.

claim: HeLa cells expressing Cx26A88V were exposed to 200 µM CBF in control aCSF for 15 min as a control, followed by 30 min of washing.
source: HeLa cells expressing Cx26A88V were exposed to 200 µM CBF in control aCSF for 15 min, followed by 30 min of washing.
evidence: This describes the control experimental protocol.

claim: A zero Ca2+ positive control was performed to ensure functional connexin hemichannels were being expressed.
source: A zero Ca2+ positive control was also performed to ensure functional connexin hemichannels were being expressed.
evidence: This describes the rationale for the positive control experiment.

claim: Cx26A88V expressing HeLa cells were exposed to 200 µM CBF in zero Ca2+ aCSF for 10 min, followed by control aCSF with 200 µM CBF for 5 min and 30 min of washing with aCSF.
source: Cx26A88V expressing HeLa cells were exposed to 200 µM CBF in zero Ca2+ aCSF for 10 min. This was followed by control aCSF with 200 µM CBF for 5 min and 30 min of washing with aCSF.
evidence: This describes the positive control experimental protocol.

claim: Cells were imaged by epifluorescence using a Scientifica Slice Scope with specific imaging equipment.
source: For each condition cells were imaged by epifluorescence (Scientifica Slice Scope, Cairn Research OptoLED illumination, 60× water Olympus immersion objective, NA 1.0, Hamamatsu ImageEM EMCCD camera, Metafluor software).
evidence: This describes the imaging equipment and methods used.

claim: The extent of dye loading was measured by drawing a region of interest (ROI) around individual cells and calculating the mean pixel intensity for the ROI using ImageJ.
source: Using ImageJ, the extent of dye loading was measured by drawing a region of interest (ROI) around individual cells and calculating the mean pixel intensity for the ROI.
evidence: This describes the image analysis method used.

claim: The mean pixel intensity of background fluorescence was measured in a representative ROI and subtracted from the measures obtained from the cells.
source: The mean pixel intensity of the background fluorescence was also measured in a representative ROI, and this value was subtracted from the measures obtained from the cells.
evidence: This describes the background correction method used in image analysis.

claim: All displayed images have the mean intensity of background pixels subtracted from every pixel of the image.
source: All of the images displayed in the figures reflect this procedure in that the mean intensity of the pixels in a representative background ROI has been subtracted from every pixel of the image.
evidence: This describes the image processing applied to all displayed figures.

claim: The analysis of the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26A88V was performed as five independent repetitions in which at least 40 cells were measured in each condition.
source: The analysis of the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26A88V was performed as five independent repetitions in which at least 40 cells were measured in each condition, and the mean pixel intensities plotted as cumulative probability distributions.
evidence: This describes the experimental replication and sample size used.

claim: Mean pixel intensities were plotted as cumulative probability distributions for the CO2 sensitivity analysis.
source: The analysis of the CO2 sensitivity of Cx26A88V was performed as five independent repetitions in which at least 40 cells were measured in each condition, and the mean pixel intensities plotted as cumulative probability distributions.
evidence: This describes the data presentation method used.

claim: Zero Ca2+ conditions open connexin hemichannels.
source: A zero Ca2+ positive control was also performed to ensure functional connexin hemichannels were being expressed.
evidence: This is implied by the use of zero Ca2+ as a positive control for hemichannel opening, drawing on established knowledge about connexin hemichannel regulation.
